questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, non-tender, and rubbery. Dark-field microscopy of serous exudate shows motile corkscrew-shaped organisms. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: This is primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum). Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the treatment of choice for primary syphilis. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with verrucous, warty plaques on the lower leg with black dots on the surface. KOH mount shows 'copper penny' or 'medlar bodies' (muriform cells). The causative organism is most likely:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis (chromomycosis) is caused by dematiaceous (melanised) fungi, most commonly Fonsecaea pedrosoi in India. The pathognomonic finding is muriform (sclerotic) cells—thick-walled brown cells dividing in two planes, seen in tissue sections.

questions.q: A 22-year-old female presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and a thickened greater auricular nerve. Slit-skin smear is negative. Skin biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytic cuffing in the dermis, but no AFB. What is the leprosy classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) features: few well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, thickened peripheral nerves, negative slit-skin smear, and well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytic cuffing on biopsy with no bacilli.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin with a positive Nikolsky sign being absent. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense bullae on urticarial bases in elderly, Nikolsky sign is negative, and DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (lamina lucida). The target antigen is BPAG2 (collagen XVII, 180 kDa).

questions.q: A 60-year-old male with a 20-year history of psoriasis develops a tender, erythematous nodule on the pinna that discharges white chalky material. Which complication of long-term psoriasis treatment is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Cyclosporine causes hyperuricemia by reducing uric acid excretion in the kidneys, leading to gouty tophi. A chalky discharge from an ear nodule is characteristic of tophaceous gout. This is a known adverse effect requiring monitoring of uric acid levels.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the buttocks. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. He reports similar episodes 4 times in the last year, often preceded by stress. What is the drug of choice for suppression of recurrences?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days
Valacyclovir 500 mg once daily for 12 months
questions.exp: This is recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2). For suppressive therapy in patients with frequent recurrences (≥6/year), valacyclovir 500 mg once daily is preferred for 12 months. It reduces recurrences by ~70–80% and also reduces transmission.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with malar erythema, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis, and a 'butterfly rash.' ANA is strongly positive (1:1280, speckled pattern). Anti-dsDNA antibodies are elevated. Which antibody is most specific for this condition?
questions.exp: Anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibodies are the most specific antibody for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with ~99% specificity, though sensitivity is only 25–30%. Anti-dsDNA is both sensitive and specific and correlates with disease activity and nephritis.

questions.q: A 32-year-old male presents with a 3 cm non-tender ulcer with undermined, ragged, violaceous edges on the lower leg. He has a history of Crohn's disease. Cultures are negative. Skin biopsy shows sterile neutrophilic infiltrate. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) presents with painful ulcers with undermined violaceous edges, sterile neutrophilic infiltrate, and is associated with IBD, RA, and haematological conditions. It demonstrates pathergy. Treatment: systemic corticosteroids or cyclosporine.

questions.q: A 19-year-old female presents with intensely pruritic vesicles and papules over the extensor aspects of elbows, knees, buttocks, and scalp. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillary tips. Treatment: dapsone for rapid symptomatic relief + strict gluten-free diet for long-term remission and cancer risk reduction.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent papule with telangiectasias on the nose, present for 2 years. The lesion bleeds easily on minor trauma. Histology shows palisading nuclei at the periphery of tumour islands with retraction artefact. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. Nodular BCC presents as a pearly papule with telangiectasias and rolled borders. Histology shows basaloid islands with peripheral palisading and cleft artefact (retraction). Associated with UV exposure and PTCH1 mutation.

questions.q: A 40-year-old construction worker presents with painful fissuring and scaling of bilateral palms that worsens in winter. Patch testing reveals positive reaction to potassium dichromate (+++). What is the occupational allergen most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Cement contains hexavalent chromium (chromate), the most common cause of occupational allergic contact dermatitis in construction workers. Patch testing with potassium dichromate is strongly positive. Avoidance and ferrous sulfate-added cement help prevent sensitization.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male (CD4 count 80 cells/µL) presents with verrucous, crusted hyperkeratotic plaques over hands and feet with innumerable mites on scraping. He reports that his household contacts have mild pruritus. What type of scabies does he have?
questions.exp: Crusted (Norwegian) scabies occurs in immunocompromised individuals (HIV, transplant, elderly). Hyperkeratotic plaques harbour millions of mites (vs. 10–15 in ordinary scabies), making it highly contagious. Treatment: oral ivermectin + topical permethrin.

questions.q: A 6-year-old girl presents with honey-coloured crusted lesions around the mouth and nose that started as vesicles. Culture grows coagulase-positive Staphylococcus aureus. Which toxin is responsible for the skin separation in the bullous form?
questions.exp: Bullous impetigo and Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) are caused by exfoliative toxins A and B (serine proteases) that cleave desmoglein-1 in the granular layer, causing superficial blistering. ETA is encoded chromosomally; ETB is plasmid-encoded.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with progressive thickening of the fingers and skin tightness extending to the forearms. She has Raynaud's phenomenon and dysphagia. ANA is positive with anti-centromere antibody pattern. Which internal organ is LEAST commonly affected in her condition?
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST syndrome) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies. Scleroderma renal crisis (with hypertension and microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and anti-topoisomerase-I (Scl-70), NOT limited disease. Lung and oesophagus involvement occurs in lcSSc.

questions.q: During a leprosy reaction, a patient develops acute tender erythematous nodules on the trunk and limbs with fever and joint pains. Histology shows neutrophilic infiltrate in the dermis. The leprosy type is most likely:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 lepra reaction) occurs in lepromatous (LL) and borderline lepromatous (BL) leprosy. It is an immune complex (Type III) hypersensitivity reaction. Treatment: thalidomide (males) or prednisolone + clofazimine.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the extensor surfaces. Auspitz sign is positive. She is 10 weeks pregnant. Which treatment is absolutely contraindicated?
questions.exp: Acitretin is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy (Category X) as it is highly teratogenic, causing craniofacial, cardiovascular, and CNS defects. Women must avoid pregnancy during treatment and for 3 years after stopping. NB-UVB is safe in pregnancy.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with hypopigmented macules on the upper back that show yellow-green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. KOH examination of scales shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (Pityrosporum). KOH mount shows hyphae (spaghetti) and round yeast cells (meatballs) = 'spaghetti and meatballs'. Wood's lamp: yellow-green fluorescence. Treatment: topical selenium sulfide, azoles, or oral itraconazole.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman presents with flaccid bullae, erosions, and crusts over the face, scalp, and trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition giving a 'chicken-wire' or 'fish-net' pattern. What is the target antigen?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) targets desmoglein-3 (mucosal type) and in extensive disease also desmoglein-1 (skin type). Antibodies disrupt desmosomal adhesion, causing suprabasal acantholysis. DIF shows intercellular IgG in chicken-wire pattern. Treatment: high-dose corticosteroids ± rituximab.

questions.q: A 55-year-old chronic smoker presents with a firm, flesh-coloured to yellowish plaque on the lower lip for 8 months. Biopsy shows dyskeratosis and squamous cell proliferation. This is most likely:
opts: Leukoplakia progressing to squamous cell carcinoma
questions.exp: Oral leukoplakia on the lip of a chronic smoker with dyskeratosis on biopsy is a premalignant condition that can progress to SCC. Risk factors: tobacco, alcohol, HPV. Biopsy with histopathology is essential for grading dysplasia and deciding treatment (excision, laser, or close surveillance).

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with grouped painless papules with central umbilication on the face and neck. He is HIV positive with CD4 count of 150. What is the treatment of choice for widespread lesions?
opts: Curettage or cryotherapy of individual lesions
Antiretroviral therapy (ART) to restore immune function
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (MCV) in HIV patients becomes extensive when CD4 falls below 200. The most effective treatment is ART, which restores immune function and leads to spontaneous resolution. Lesions on the face in an HIV+ adult should prompt CD4 count evaluation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male farmer presents with a painless nodule on the dorsum of the right hand that developed after a thorn prick. It ulcerated, and new nodules appeared in a linear pattern ascending up the forearm following lymphatics. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) presents with a primary ulcerated nodule at the inoculation site followed by secondary nodules along lymphatics (sporotrichoid spread). Diagnostic pearl: 'lymphocutaneous pattern.' Treatment: oral itraconazole 200 mg/day for 3–6 months.

questions.q: A 16-year-old male presents with comedones, papules, pustules, and nodules on the face and back for 2 years. He has severe nodulocystic acne with scarring. After failing topical retinoids and antibiotics, he is started on isotretinoin. What is the most important monitoring parameter?
opts: Liver function tests and serum lipids
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause hepatotoxicity (elevated transaminases) and hypertriglyceridemia. Baseline and monthly monitoring of LFTs and fasting lipid profile is mandatory. Other monitoring: serum β-hCG (females), mood assessment (depression risk), and mucocutaneous side effects.

questions.q: A 70-year-old male presents with a reddish-brown plaque on the right lower leg with haemosiderin deposits, lipodermatosclerosis, and a shallow ulcer above the medial malleolus. Ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI) is 0.9. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Venous leg ulcers present above the medial malleolus with lipodermatosclerosis and haemosiderin staining. ABPI ≥0.8 is required before applying compression. Four-layer compression bandaging is the gold standard treatment, promoting healing by reducing venous hypertension.

questions.q: A 30-year-old female presents with violaceous, flat-topped, polygonal papules on the flexor aspect of wrists with Wickham's striae visible. Buccal mucosa shows white reticular lesions. What is the most likely mechanism?
opts: CD8+ T-cell mediated cytotoxicity against keratinocytes
questions.exp: Lichen planus (LP) is a T-cell mediated (Type IV) autoimmune condition. CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes target basal keratinocytes expressing altered self-antigens, causing cell death (colloid/Civatte bodies). Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ is characteristic on histology.

questions.q: A 2-year-old child presents with a port-wine stain (PWS) on the right side of the face following the V1/V2 distribution of the trigeminal nerve. Which associated condition must be ruled out?
questions.exp: Sturge-Weber syndrome (encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis) is associated with a facial PWS in the V1 distribution, ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma, epilepsy, intellectual disability, and glaucoma. All children with V1 PWS need neuroimaging and ophthalmology evaluation. Caused by somatic GNAQ mutation.

questions.q: A 38-year-old female presents with episodic facial flushing, erythema, telangiectasias, and papulopustules on the cheeks and nose for 3 years. There are no comedones. Which Demodex-targeting treatment has been recently approved?
questions.exp: Topical ivermectin 1% cream (Soolantra) targets Demodex mites, which play a role in rosacea pathogenesis. It is approved for papulopustular rosacea. Brimonidine and oxymetazoline treat erythema. Oral doxycycline (sub-antimicrobial) reduces inflammation. Metronidazole is a classic topical option.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with sharply demarcated circular patches of hair loss on the scalp with no scarring. The affected skin appears smooth. Hair pull test at the periphery is positive. Which histological feature is pathognomonic?
opts: Trichomalacia and melanin casts in hair follicles
'Swarm of bees' pattern — peribulbar lymphocytic infiltrate
questions.exp: Alopecia areata shows a characteristic 'swarm of bees' peribulbar lymphocytic infiltrate targeting the hair bulb matrix. The attack focuses on the anagen bulb. It is a non-scarring alopecia with a positive hair pull test at margins. Associated with thyroid disease and other autoimmune conditions.

questions.q: A 19-year-old university student presents with small white-grey lice eggs (nits) firmly adherent to hair shafts close to the scalp. She has been sharing combs. What is the drug of choice?
questions.exp: Pediculus humanus capitis (head lice) — first-line treatment is permethrin 1% rinse (left on for 10 min), which is pediculicidal and ovicidal. Repeat after 7–10 days. Lindane is avoided due to neurotoxicity. Oral ivermectin is used for treatment failures.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with wrinkling, yellowing, and deep furrowing of the skin on the back of the neck and behind the ears, giving a 'cobblestone' appearance. He is a heavy smoker and a chronic outdoor worker. This condition is called:
opts: Favre-Racouchot syndrome (nodular elastosis with cysts and comedones)
questions.exp: Favre-Racouchot syndrome (solar elastosis with comedones) is caused by chronic sun and tobacco exposure causing massive degeneration of dermal elastic tissue (solar elastosis) with open comedones and cysts on the face and neck. Treatment: tretinoin and comedone extraction.

questions.q: A patient with gonorrhoea is treated with ceftriaxone. 3 days later, urethral discharge persists. NAAT confirms Chlamydia trachomatis co-infection. Which drug is most appropriate to add?
questions.exp: Non-gonococcal urethritis (NGU) due to Chlamydia trachomatis is treated with azithromycin 1 g single dose or doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days. The CDC/WHO recommends empirically treating gonorrhoea with ceftriaxone + azithromycin to cover likely Chlamydia co-infection.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male is being treated for multibacillary leprosy with WHO-MDT. After 6 months, he develops sudden onset of painful tender enlargement of the ulnar nerve at the elbow with clawing of the ring and little fingers. What is this complication called and how is it managed?
opts: Type 1 reaction — treat with prednisolone 40–60 mg/day and continue MDT
Type 2 reaction — treat with thalidomide 100–300 mg/day
Silent neuritis — treat with physiotherapy alone
questions.exp: Reversal (Type 1) lepra reactions occur in borderline leprosy due to delayed hypersensitivity (CMI upgrade), causing acute neuritis and new skin lesions. Urgent high-dose prednisolone (40–60 mg/day, tapering over 3–6 months) is essential to prevent permanent nerve damage. MDT must be continued.
